steps.note: LLaMA-Factory based, in training/ of QwenAudio/Fun-Audio-Chat. The main line has since moved to MiniCPM-o 4.5, which already runs in full duplex.
steps.title: Check Fun-Audio-Chat's training code (first plan)

steps.note: All 14 setups rescored; Fun hand-off only 68, or 78 with the 10 benchmark errors counted
steps.title: Rescore all setups, benchmark errors counted as passed

steps.note: envs/funtrain: torch 2.8 (cu126), transformers 4.52.3, PEFT 0.17.1, DeepSpeed 0.17.3, LLaMA-Factory 0.9.4.dev0, pyarrow 18.1. No flash-attn yet; using sdpa.
steps.title: Training environment on the server (Fun-Audio-Chat)

steps.note: Both train on 4 cards with the speech head off. LoRA + ZeRO-3: 10.5 GB per card, 3.5 s per step of 4 samples. QLoRA: 11.5 GB, 1.1 s. This showed LoRA fits on the 16 GB cards; MiniCPM-o still needs its own smoke test (step 10).
steps.title: Smoke test on Fun-Audio-Chat: LoRA + ZeRO-3 and QLoRA

steps.note: Main line moved to MiniCPM-o, which already runs in full duplex. Its duplex sequence is one unit per second of audio, with <|listen|> / <|speak|>, <|chunk_eos|> and <|turn_eos|>; the language model (Qwen3-8B) can take LoRA. Samples are stored model-neutral, so the data serves either model.
steps.title: Switch to MiniCPM-o 4.5: full-duplex format and LoRA feasibility

steps.note: 17,480 tools (When2Call 3,267, ToolACE 14,213); 126 FDB-like tools removed. The held-out split uses the domain labels from the next step.
steps.title: Tool pool and held-out tool split

steps.note: 17,397 labeled (83 dropped: answer outside the label set). 14,168 suit voice: 11,312 lookup, 1,515 search, 1,341 action. Held out six whole domains (health, food, calendar, weather, real_estate, jobs): 1,662 tools, 276 of them action; 12,506 tools left for training.
steps.title: Tool weight labels (lookup, search, action)

steps.note: Done: 154 batches written and checked, then three fix passes. Third pass (after the stratified review): dropped 996 samples that read API values aloud (Qwen3-14B proposed, Claude confirmed), all 427 first-round ask rewrites, 338 asks and 59 chats that failed a Claude review of every ask and chat, 7 card numbers and 5 reviewed leaks; added 835 new asks written and reviewed by Claude. Final set: 14,076 samples (train 12,686, dev 694, test 696); call 33.0%, handoff 31.0%, ask 15.7%, chat 10.6%, split 9.6%; 1,945 filler, 728 self-correction. Section C passes.
steps.title: Requests and targets (fast tools in the frontend, the rest handed off)

steps.note: Done with Kokoro (18 English voices, 16 kHz): every user turn of the 14,076 samples, earlier context turns included, 22,955 WAVs. ISO dates read as spoken dates; one 0.5-2 s pause at a phrase boundary in 30% of requests.
steps.title: TTS, with pauses at phrase boundaries

steps.note: Format proven by the feasibility test (duplex target right 52-54/60 vs 20/60 untrained; results fed back as text units told with a value 30/34). All 14,076 samples are now built as duplex sequences (median 1,202 tokens, max 3,874; 16 GB of audio embeddings), with the 34 banned decoder tokens the targets use listed for inference. Left: the general-dialogue mix and the training run itself, which waits for your go-ahead.
steps.title: MiniCPM-o duplex format, training setup and smoke test

steps.note: Claude reviewed the 280-sample stratified review (target right 97.5%, fully correct 89.6%); you decided the four problem groups; the third fix round applied them to the whole set with a Claude review of every ask and chat and of every flagged API-value request. The final set passes section C.
steps.title: Your review of the data
Untrained MiniCPM-o baseline
steps.note: Done in text chat mode (full duplex has no tool-call path; TTS not run yet): official MiniCPM-o 4.5 code, fast tools + spawn_thinking, 692 test samples. Target accuracy 59.2%: call 61.2%, handoff 84.5%, ask 13.8%, split 49.3%, chat 62.4%. It over-hands-off (75 call and 25 chat items sent to the backend), almost never asks, and says nothing when it hands off (0 of 198). Reporting a backend result already works: 31/31 right after the handoff, 30/31 after an unrelated exchange. To rerun on speech after TTS.
Learning curve on 25%, 50% and 100% of the data to see whether more data would help.

Evaluate: FDB-v3 in full duplex, held-out tools, chat regression
